the IFT of interleaved composities is dependent on the areal density, fibre diameter, anisotropy of the veil, and the type of resin used.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the influence of nonwovens on IFT is a function of the veil architecture and the properties of the fibres and matrix.
the IFT of interleaved compositesis determined by the veil coverage of the crack path, which is a function of both the veil areal density and its architecture.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

for both PPS and PEEK veils, the mode I and II IFT increase with increasing areal density of veil up to a point, beyond which the IFT is insensitive to the areal density; for the same areal density, mode I IFT increases with decreasing fibre diameter.
the mode I and mode III IFT of a nonwoven interleaved composite depends on the mean fibre coverage of the veil.
for a given veil architecture, the IFT is proportional to the fraction of the crack front that does not contain fibres, and for a given veil weight, the IFT depends only weakly on the architecture.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IFT of interleaved compositess is controlled by the veil areal density, and the IFT of a given veil is independent of the matrix material.
nonwoven veils can be used to improve the interlaminar toughness of composites without significantly degrading the in-plane strength.
nonwoven veils are effective in increasing IFT of laminates, and the effect is largely determined by the areal density.
